acceptance_criteria.criterion: ledger_get_repository_context returns a structured response with repository_name, repository_id, repository_label, total_projects, strategic_vision, projects[], and relevant_insights[].
When a declared repository has multiple folder_names, projects from ALL matching folder names are aggregated into a single response, sorted by date_created descending.
When no registry match exists, the tool returns null for repository_id, repository_label, and strategic_vision, and reads projects from the single derived folder name only.
max_projects parameter caps the returned project list (default: 5).
include_insights: false omits the relevant_insights[] from the response.
listProjectsByFolderNames(["a"]) reads only the a/ namespace directory, not the entire ledger root.
listProjectsByFolderNames returns an empty array gracefully for non-existent folder names.
include_insights: false returns an empty relevant_insights[] array in the response (field always present to preserve response shape consistency).

comments.note: No blocking issues — code is clean and consistent with codebase conventions across all four review dimensions (maintainability, best practices, performance, future context).

Fix-Forward applied in mcp-server/src/tools/repository-context.ts: updated the include_insights Zod field .describe() string from 'Set to false to omit insights and reduce response size.' to 'Set to false to return an empty relevant_insights[] array and reduce response size.' — aligns the schema description with the actual contract (empty array returned, field always present) to prevent consumer confusion.

The cwd_path → repository_name derivation (constructing a synthetic plan path `${args.cwd_path}/docs/agents/plans/synthetic-slug` and calling deriveRepoName()) is a functional indirection. It works correctly because deriveRepoName() just walks 4 levels up from the plan path, and the synthetic slug is never used. However, the comment on line 94-96 documents this clearly. A future refactor could expose a dedicated resolveFolderNameFromCwd(workspaceRoot) helper in ledger-root.ts to eliminate the synthetic path construction — low priority, not blocking.

The safeListRepositoryInsights helper uses a bare catch{} to swallow all errors from listInsights() when called with scope='repository'. This is appropriate: repository insights are best-effort enrichment and a SLUG_REGEX validation failure (for e.g. 'unknown' repository names) should not surface as a tool error. The pattern is intentional and correctly documented in the JSDoc.

Global and repository insights are concatenated without deduplication ([...globalInsights, ...repoInsights]). If a future knowledge-base workflow allows the same insight to appear in both stores, the Planner may see duplicates. Not a current issue — global and repository stores are disjoint by schema — but worth a comment near the concat. Low risk, low priority.

Key design decisions: (1) listProjectsByFolderNames is O(folders × projects) not O(all repos) — targeted read, not full ledger scan. (2) Cross-folder aggregation only triggers when a registry entry declares multiple folder_names. (3) total_projects reflects ALL discovered projects, not the max_projects-capped subset — gives Planner accurate context on how many plans exist. (4) include_insights: false returns an empty relevant_insights[] rather than omitting the field, preserving response shape consistency.
